sections.html:
The Tax Office has two departments, both at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. Property gets listed, appraised and assessed by the Assessor. Collections handles billing and payment for real estate, personal property and delinquent motor vehicles.

Write to PO Box 1557, Raeford, NC 28376, or call 910-875-8751. The county's roll covers about 28,000 parcels of land, 700 businesses and 40,000 motor vehicles across roughly 390 square miles of land.

For context on pricing, Population climbed from 52,082 in the 2020 count to an estimated 56,939 in July 2025, in 22,440 housing units. Roughly 73.0 percent of homes are owner occupied, with a midpoint value of $219,300. Builders took out 558 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: Rates and fees on the bill
sections.html:
Four pieces can make up a bill: the county rate, a city rate, a fire district rate and a solid waste fee. Each rate is charged per $100 of value. City properties skip the fire district tax and the solid waste fee.

Sample Hoke County bill lines
Line on the billRate or fee
Hoke County rate.73 per $100 of value
City of Raeford rate.48 per $100 of value
North Raeford fire district rate.10 per $100 of value
Solid waste fee$130.00 per unit in the sample bill

No two fire districts charge the same. The Tax Office has a sheet naming the district for your parcel, and it can confirm the current Raeford rate for a house inside city limits.

The last countywide revaluation took effect January 1, 2022, with notices going to all taxpayers on February 3, 2022. The next is set for January 1, 2030, and work starts two years before.

Eight years is the longest gap allowed between reappraisals under G.S. 105-286. Meanwhile your real property value is pegged to the January 1, 2022 market unless you build something new or the parcel changes. The assessor can show how a sale price stacks up against your 2022 value.

An appraisal sets each owner's share of the taxes that support schools, roads, parks, public health, libraries, police and fire protection. What you pay depends on your value and the rates set each year by elected county and city or town officials.

Send the Notice of Appeal of Assessment to the Tax Assessor ahead of the equalization board's adjournment. Newspaper and web notices announce the date, and the assessor's office will confirm it by phone. Your appeal must be in before then, so mark the date once the notice appears.

  • Each parcel needs its own form, signed by the owner or a representative: an attorney, or an attorney in fact with a power of attorney if the owner is not a corporation.
  • Evidence can be an appraisal, sales of similar properties, income and expense statements or replacement cost. Send copies with the form.
  • You must prove the value was well above true market value on the January 1, 2022 valuation date.
  • The board sets a hearing date and tells you. You can attend or send counsel.

An appraisal already handed over in an informal appeal does not have to be resent. If the county board does not settle it, you can go on to the Property Tax Commission by giving written notice within 30 days of the mailed decision. See G.S. 105-290.

Taxes fall due September 1. G.S. 105-360 sets face value for payment before January 6, a 2 percent charge from then through February 1, and three quarters of a percent for each month afterward.

Online payment is available, and Collections takes billing questions. Mailed payments count as of the USPS postmark, so hold on to the envelope. Counties may offer prepayment discounts, and Collections can tell you if Hoke does.

A lien attaches to the parcel under G.S. 105-355 as of the listing date, and the county may foreclose in the court where the land lies. Auctions take place at the courthouse door, and a person who redeems ahead of confirmation owes the tax with penalties, interest and costs. See G.S. 105-374.

The state's three programs are the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferral, and each owner picks one. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor.

For 2026 the base income limit is $38,800 and the circuit breaker's upper tier is $58,200. June 1 before the tax year is the filing cutoff. Selling triggers the deferred tax under the circuit breaker, which is worth raising with your attorney before listing. See NCDOR Form AV-9.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill when you sell
sections.html:
Ask Collections for a payoff covering the current and prior years. The lien runs from the listing date, so a current-year bill left unpaid has to be cleared at closing.

  • Let the closing attorney pay taxes out of proceeds.
  • Outside Raeford, expect a fire district tax and a solid waste fee on the bill.
  • Confirm any exclusion filing is current before the sale.
  • Keep the 2022 value notice where you can find it.

Phone Collections at 910-875-8751 early, and refresh any payoff quoted weeks ahead, because the figure changes once penalties start in January. Even a quick cash closing pays the taxes from your proceeds, so line up the number first.

sections.h2: Reading your bill before you list
sections.html:
Take last year's bill and go line by line. Every parcel carries the county rate, but a Raeford rate appears only inside the city. Outside it, you will see a fire district rate and the solid waste fee. A line that seems off deserves a call to the Tax Office before a buyer's attorney notices.

Next, check the value. The 2022 revaluation fixed values at the January 1, 2022 market, so your assessment may differ from what a buyer will pay now. That gap alone is no basis for an appeal, which must show the value was too high on the 2022 date.

The tax year looks like this for a seller. Pay the September 1 bill by January 6 and nothing extra applies. Later, 2 percent and then three quarters of a percent monthly pile on. Since the lien dates from listing, a buyer's side will want the account paid or cleared at closing before a contract goes through.

Before the first showing, collect your parcel information, latest bill, any exclusion filing and 2022 value notice. With those in hand Collections can quote a payoff fast, and a tax question will not slow the closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Hoke County Tax Office?
faqs.a: Both the Assessor and Collections are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. Write to PO Box 1557, Raeford, NC 28376, or call 910-875-8751.

faqs.q: When is the next Hoke County revaluation?
faqs.a: Set for January 1, 2030, with work starting two years earlier. The previous revaluation was effective January 1, 2022, and notices went out February 3, 2022.

faqs.q: What is the Hoke County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's sample bill shows a county rate of .73 per $100, a Raeford rate of .48 and a North Raeford fire district rate of .10. A solid waste fee can apply outside city limits, so ask for the current rate sheet.

faqs.q: What do I file to contest a value?
faqs.a: File one Notice of Appeal of Assessment per parcel with the Tax Assessor, plus evidence like appraisals or comparable sales, before the equalization board adjourns. Newspaper and website notices give that date.

faqs.q: Does Hoke County have a fire district tax?
faqs.a: Yes, outside city limits. The rate depends on the district where the property sits and is added to the county rate.
